Do not cite references absent from the current LOG DATA; do not invent events to bridge batches. Use only per-event evidence shown in this call for individual chronology and endpoint attribution. An aggregate is not an individual Zeek flow. This observation is not proof of attacker intent or intrusion. Other source records exist outside this batch and are independently summarized in the unified Python baseline.

CITATION POLICY: Cite ONLY the canonical [E###] tag immediately preceding each input record. Source-origin E### IDs are withheld from the model and remain in the analyst manifest. Never invent an E### reference or use internal/source-level IDs as citation labels.

DRAFT COMPLETENESS: Include all required ## headings, one clearly scoped report confidence level. Give at most THREE representative evidence-linked bullets per narrative section, no more than THREE real source-timestamp timeline rows, and at most FOUR evidence explanations. The program adds the COMPLETE evidence timeline independently. Never use "...", "continue for all events", filler rows or implied missing content. Unknown details must be explicitly called unknown, not guessed.

ZEEK FACT BOUNDARIES: A raw conn.log row represents an individual flow record; one dst_port=65535 row is NOT evidence that all ports were scanned. Use full-source counts ONLY from the verified-in-input aggregate and distinguish that derived count from sample rows. Zeek REJ is a connection state, not proof of firewall blocking. Never assert all sampled rows use one source port unless verified.
